name: ANSI/IEEE terminal with wire number change symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented round terminal at which the wire number changes, with a different number on each side.
description: The publisher's IEEE terminal preview includes a round terminal form at which the wire number changes. It is used at boundaries such as panel to field interfaces, where the panel wiring uses one numbering scheme and the field cable cores another.

This illustration is independent and not the IEEE graphic. The electrical connection is continuous; only the identifier changes. Readers tracing a circuit must follow the number change, and the terminal plan should list both numbers against the terminal.
readingNotes: Follow the new wire number beyond the terminal.
Check both numbers appear on the terminal plan.
drawingChecklist: Show both wire numbers at the terminal.
List both on the terminal plan.
Use the change form only at genuine boundaries.
distinction: The change form renumbers the wire; the standard wire number form keeps one number through the terminal.
